text:
Muscle lactate production increases when glycolytic flux outpaces mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation, as in high-intensity exercise, hypoxia/ischemia, or impaired mitochondrial function, forcing pyruvate to be converted to lactate via lactate dehydrogenase to regenerate NAD+ and sustain glycolysis. The team note is incorrect: lactate is formed from pyruvate, not when pyruvate formation is blocked—blocking pyruvate formation would reduce lactate production.  
CONFIDENCE: 95
